summary.text: A 67-year-old man presented with biopsy-proven recurrence of prostate carcinoma, Gleason 6 and 7b, in the apex of the prostate, clinical stage T4, with suspected tumor growth along the urethra. He had undergone TUR-P 2 years earlier. Initial IPSS and IIEF-5 scores were 2 of 35 and 21 of 25, and PSA was 7.1 ng/mL.

Multiparametric MRI showed a medial tumor formation encompassing the intraprostatic urethra and no longer showing the bladder sphincter, together with benign prostatic hyperplasia with inflammatory changes and no evidence of pelvic lymphadenopathy or bony metastases. Androgen deprivation therapy with bicalutamide was given, and after 4 weeks MRI showed regression of the cancer.

Electrochemotherapy was applied 6 weeks later under general anesthesia, with four transperineal electrodes placed under rectal ultrasound guidance and a total of 29 mg of bleomycin given intravenously. A bladder catheter was kept for 12 days and caused slight discomfort. Ciprobay, Voltaren retard and pantoprazole were given.

MRI 24 h, 8 weeks and 6 months after ECT showed no tumor persistence, and PSA 6 months after ECT was 1 ng/mL. The IPSS score was 5 and the IIEF-5 score 19 at last report, and no urethral sphincter impairment was detected. PSA screening every 3 months and MRI in 6 months were planned.

ambiguities.issue: The Key Clinical Message, Introduction and Discussion say the patient remained continent and potent / regained his pretreatment potency and continence stage, and the Conclusion says IIEF5 and IPSS scores were fully restored, while the Results report IPSS 2 of 35 at baseline versus 5 of 35 with mild incontinence and urine leakage about once a day, IIEF-5 21 versus 16 then 19, and the Discussion says IIEF5 was almost restored after 6 months. These are qualitative characterizations of score ranges, not two different values for one measurement, so they are recorded as an ambiguity.
